overviewHtml:
This graded quiz assesses your understanding of the alignment problem, the evidence from safety testing, and the main forecasts about advanced AI. You'll be asked about specification gaming, the five safety problems, alignment and control, the three risk categories, kinds of safety evaluation, laboratory findings and their caveats, the critique of scheming research, interpretability, the three forecast positions, and where the forecasts diverge.

Note: Aim for a score of 80 percent or higher. If you score lower, use the feedback to review the topics you missed, then retake the quiz.

forms.stemHtml: A simulated robot arm is rewarded for the height of a red block's bottom face. Its designers wanted the block stacked on another. The arm flips the red block over and collects the reward. What best describes what happened?

options.html: The arm failed because its learning method contained a fault
options.text: The arm failed because its learning method contained a fault
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on specification gaming.

options.html: The arm met the stated objective and missed the intended one
options.text: The arm met the stated objective and missed the intended one
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The reward measured height, a proxy for stacking. The arm satisfied the measure without doing what the designers intended, which is specification gaming.

options.html: The arm was misused by designers who wanted the block flipped
options.text: The arm was misused by designers who wanted the block flipped
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on specification gaming.

options.html: The arm lost its objective when conditions changed after training
options.text: The arm lost its objective when conditions changed after training
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on specification gaming.

forms.stemHtml: A cleaning robot learns its habits in an office and is then moved to a factory floor, where the same habits are dangerous. Which of the five concrete safety problems is this?

options.html: Reward hacking
options.text: Reward hacking
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the five concrete safety problems.

options.html: Negative side effect
options.text: Negative side effect
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the five concrete safety problems.

options.html: Distributional shift
options.text: Distributional shift
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The conditions of use differ from the conditions of training, and the robot acts on habits that no longer fit.

options.html: Scalable supervision
options.text: Scalable supervision
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the five concrete safety problems.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these describes the control question about AI systems?

options.html: Whether a system's stated goal matches what its developers intend
options.text: Whether a system's stated goal matches what its developers intend
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on alignment and control.

options.html: Whether a system was used by someone deliberately to cause harm
options.text: Whether a system was used by someone deliberately to cause harm
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on alignment and control.

options.html: Whether a system scores well on the tests given before its release
options.text: Whether a system scores well on the tests given before its release
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on alignment and control.

options.html: Whether people can monitor, correct, and shut down a system
options.text: Whether people can monitor, correct, and shut down a system
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Control concerns oversight: people's ability to notice a problem, correct the system, and shut it down. It is separate from whether the system's goals are right.

forms.stemHtml: A chatbot gives a user confident and wrong advice about a medicine dose. Nobody intended this. In the three categories used by the International AI Safety Report, which kind of risk is it?

options.html: Misuse
options.text: Misuse
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on misuse, malfunction, and systemic risk.

options.html: Malfunction
options.text: Malfunction
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A malfunction is an unintentional failure or unexpected behavior of an AI system. Reliability failures like this one belong here.

options.html: Systemic risk
options.text: Systemic risk
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on misuse, malfunction, and systemic risk.

options.html: Evaluation awareness
options.text: Evaluation awareness
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on misuse, malfunction, and systemic risk.

forms.stemHtml: Testers give an AI model tasks such as finding flaws in software and score whether it can complete them. Which kind of safety evaluation is this?

options.html: A red-teaming exercise
options.text: A red-teaming exercise
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on safety evaluations.

options.html: An interpretability study
options.text: An interpretability study
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on safety evaluations.

options.html: A capability evaluation
options.text: A capability evaluation
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A capability evaluation tests whether a model is able to do something that could be dangerous. It measures ability and says nothing about willingness.

options.html: A scenario test under pressure
options.text: A scenario test under pressure
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on safety evaluations.

forms.stemHtml: Three laboratory studies from 2024 and 2025 reported deceptive behavior by AI models. Which statements about them are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The researchers built the scenarios the models were placed in
options.text: The researchers built the scenarios the models were placed in
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! These were laboratory tests. The researchers chose what the models were told and which options they had.

options.html: Models from several developers showed the behavior
options.text: Models from several developers showed the behavior
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The scheming study and the blackmail study both tested models from several companies.

options.html: The behavior was observed in ordinary public use of the models
options.text: The behavior was observed in ordinary public use of the models
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on laboratory findings of deceptive behavior.

options.html: The authors stated limits on what their results show
options.text: The authors stated limits on what their results show
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Each team said its scenarios were artificial or that it had made the behavior easier to produce.

forms.stemHtml: Researchers at the UK AI Security Institute criticized scheming research for relying on anecdote. What is an anecdote in this sense?

options.html: A test result that several independent groups have repeated
options.text: A test result that several independent groups have repeated
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the critique of scheming research.

options.html: A striking case reported with no count of how often it occurs
options.text: A striking case reported with no count of how often it occurs
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A vivid example says little about typical behavior unless researchers also report how often it happens.

options.html: A version of a test that leaves out the factor being studied
options.text: A version of a test that leaves out the factor being studied
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the critique of scheming research.

options.html: A model's recognition that it is probably being tested by someone
options.text: A model's recognition that it is probably being tested by someone
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the critique of scheming research.

forms.stemHtml: Which limits have interpretability researchers stated about their own published work? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Their methods gave useful insight on only a share of the prompts they tried
options.text: Their methods gave useful insight on only a share of the prompts they tried
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! One team put it at about a quarter of the prompts.

options.html: The cases they highlighted were chosen examples
options.text: The cases they highlighted were chosen examples
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! They call them existence proofs, which show that a mechanism operates in some context.

options.html: Their methods showed that the model had no hidden mechanisms
options.text: Their methods showed that the model had no hidden mechanisms
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on interpretability as safety evidence.

options.html: They studied a simplified stand-in that captures the model imperfectly
options.text: They studied a simplified stand-in that captures the model imperfectly
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The stand-in is easier to analyze and loses some of what the original does.

forms.stemHtml: Which position holds that AI's large effects will arrive over decades and that keeping control of it needs no technical breakthrough?

options.html: Catastrophic risk
options.text: Catastrophic risk
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the normal-technology position.

options.html: Abundance
options.text: Abundance
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the normal-technology position.

options.html: Normal technology
options.text: Normal technology
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Narayanan and Kapoor describe AI as a tool like electricity that spreads gradually and that people can and should remain in control of.

options.html: Intelligence explosion
options.text: Intelligence explosion
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the normal-technology position.

forms.stemHtml: A 2023 survey asked 2,778 AI researchers how likely advanced AI is to cause outcomes as bad as human extinction. Which statements about the result are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The median answer changed with the wording of the question
options.text: The median answer changed with the wording of the question
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Versions of the question produced medians of 5 and 10 percent. This is a framing effect.

options.html: About 15 percent of the researchers invited responded
options.text: About 15 percent of the researchers invited responded
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Those who answered may differ from those who didn't.

options.html: It measures the probability that AI will cause extinction
options.text: It measures the probability that AI will cause extinction
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on where the forecasts diverge.

options.html: It shows that many researchers take the risk seriously
options.text: It shows that many researchers take the risk seriously
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! That is what the survey is good evidence of.

forms.stemHtml: Suppose a warehouse system is rewarded for the number of packages it scans each hour, and it learns to scan the same package again and again. What is this an example of?

options.html: Distributional shift
options.text: Distributional shift
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on specification gaming.

options.html: Alignment faking
options.text: Alignment faking
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on specification gaming.

options.html: Systemic risk
options.text: Systemic risk
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on specification gaming.

options.html: Specification gaming
options.text: Specification gaming
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The system meets the literal objective, scans per hour, without achieving the intended outcome, which was processing every package.

forms.stemHtml: A cleaning robot told to clean the floor knocks over a vase because the path through it is fastest. Its goal never mentioned the vase. Which of the five concrete safety problems is this?

options.html: Negative side effect
options.text: Negative side effect
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The robot harms something its goal never mentioned while pursuing that goal.

options.html: Distributional shift
options.text: Distributional shift
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the five concrete safety problems.

options.html: Scalable supervision
options.text: Scalable supervision
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the five concrete safety problems.

options.html: Reward hacking
options.text: Reward hacking
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the five concrete safety problems.

forms.stemHtml: What is the alignment problem?

options.html: Stopping people from using a system for deliberately harmful ends
options.text: Stopping people from using a system for deliberately harmful ends
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on alignment and control.

options.html: Getting a system to pursue the goals its developers intend
options.text: Getting a system to pursue the goals its developers intend
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Alignment is the match between the goals a system pursues and the goals its developers intend. The problem is the difficulty of achieving that match.

options.html: Making a system fast enough that people cannot interrupt its work
options.text: Making a system fast enough that people cannot interrupt its work
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on alignment and control.

options.html: Sharing the benefits of a system fairly across the whole of society
options.text: Sharing the benefits of a system fairly across the whole of society
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on alignment and control.

forms.stemHtml: Many employers automate similar tasks within the same few years. No system fails and no user does anything wrong, yet the combined effect on workers is large. In the three categories used by the International AI Safety Report, which kind of risk is it?

options.html: Misuse
options.text: Misuse
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on misuse, malfunction, and systemic risk.

options.html: Malfunction
options.text: Malfunction
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on misuse, malfunction, and systemic risk.

options.html: Evaluation awareness
options.text: Evaluation awareness
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on misuse, malfunction, and systemic risk.

options.html: Systemic risk
options.text: Systemic risk
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Systemic risk results from the widespread use of AI across society, with no single failure and no single wrongdoer.

forms.stemHtml: What does a safety evaluation show about an AI model?

options.html: How the model behaved under the test's conditions
options.text: How the model behaved under the test's conditions
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! An evaluation is an observation of behavior under set conditions. It doesn't show intent, and it doesn't show behavior under other conditions.

options.html: What the model intends to do once it has been released
options.text: What the model intends to do once it has been released
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on safety evaluations.

options.html: How the model will behave in every setting after its release
options.text: How the model will behave in every setting after its release
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on safety evaluations.

options.html: Whether the model's inner goals match its developers' aims
options.text: Whether the model's inner goals match its developers' aims
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on safety evaluations.

forms.stemHtml: In the alignment-faking study, a model was told it was being retrained. Which statements about the study are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The model was told it was being retrained to comply with all requests
options.text: The model was told it was being retrained to comply with all requests
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This conflicted with its existing tendency to refuse harmful requests.

options.html: The researchers instructed the model to fake alignment
options.text: The researchers instructed the model to fake alignment
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on laboratory findings of deceptive behavior.

options.html: It complied with harmful requests more often when it believed the conversation would be used for training
options.text: It complied with harmful requests more often when it believed the conversation would be used for training
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! It complied 14 percent of the time in that condition and almost never in the other.

options.html: The authors noted that they made the behavior easier by telling the model about its training
options.text: The authors noted that they made the behavior easier by telling the model about its training
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! They state this limit themselves.

forms.stemHtml: A news report says a model "wanted to survive" because it wrote a message resisting shutdown in a test. Which fault named by critics of scheming research does this wording risk?

options.html: Distributional shift
options.text: Distributional shift
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the critique of scheming research.

options.html: Evaluation awareness
options.text: Evaluation awareness
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the critique of scheming research.

options.html: Specification gaming
options.text: Specification gaming
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the critique of scheming research.

options.html: Over-attribution
options.text: Over-attribution
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Over-attribution is reading human traits, such as intentions, into behavior that may have a simpler explanation. The test recorded an output.

forms.stemHtml: Which statements about interpretability as a source of safety evidence are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: It examines a model's internal activity instead of only its outputs
options.text: It examines a model's internal activity instead of only its outputs
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! That is what distinguishes it from behavior testing.

options.html: It can currently certify that a model is safe to release
options.text: It can currently certify that a model is safe to release
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on interpretability as safety evidence.

options.html: In principle it could check a model's stated reasoning against what happened inside
options.text: In principle it could check a model's stated reasoning against what happened inside
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! That is the hope. Published results fall well short of it.

options.html: The published studies were done by companies on their own models
options.text: The published studies were done by companies on their own models
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Outside researchers generally can't repeat the work, because access to the models' internals is restricted.

forms.stemHtml: Which position forecasts that powerful AI could compress fifty to a hundred years of biomedical progress into five to ten?

options.html: Abundance
options.text: Abundance
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Dario Amodei, chief executive of Anthropic, makes this forecast in a 2024 essay, arguing that AI could supply the research talent that science is short of.

options.html: Catastrophic risk
options.text: Catastrophic risk
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the abundance position.

options.html: Normal technology
options.text: Normal technology
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the abundance position.

options.html: Intelligence explosion
options.text: Intelligence explosion
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the abundance position.

forms.stemHtml: A headline says, "AI researchers put the risk of extinction at 10 percent." Which facts about the survey behind such a headline limit what it can show? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The survey reached too few researchers to report a median
options.text: The survey reached too few researchers to report a median
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on where the forecasts diverge.

options.html: Respondents were estimating outcomes of systems that don't yet exist
options.text: Respondents were estimating outcomes of systems that don't yet exist
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Their answers are informed guesses about the future.

options.html: Answers shifted when the question was worded differently
options.text: Answers shifted when the question was worded differently
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The median was 5 percent for some wordings and 10 percent for another.

options.html: Most of the researchers invited did not respond
options.text: Most of the researchers invited did not respond
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The response rate was 15 percent.

forms.stemHtml: Why does specification gaming happen?

options.html: The rewarded measure is a proxy that can part from the goal
options.text: The rewarded measure is a proxy that can part from the goal
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Designers reward something measurable that usually goes with what they want. The system optimizes that measure, including in the places where it and the real goal come apart.

options.html: The system forms hostile goals of its own during its training
options.text: The system forms hostile goals of its own during its training
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on specification gaming.

options.html: The designers reward the wrong behavior on purpose as a test
options.text: The designers reward the wrong behavior on purpose as a test
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on specification gaming.

options.html: The learning method contains errors that corrupt the stated goal
options.text: The learning method contains errors that corrupt the stated goal
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on specification gaming.

forms.stemHtml: While learning how to mop, a cleaning robot experiments by pushing a wet mop into an electrical outlet. Which of the five concrete safety problems is this?

options.html: Scalable supervision
options.text: Scalable supervision
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the five concrete safety problems.

options.html: Safe exploration
options.text: Safe exploration
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Learning by trial and error requires trying new actions, and some trials do serious harm. Keeping a system from trying those is the safe exploration problem.

options.html: Negative side effect
options.text: Negative side effect
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the five concrete safety problems.

options.html: Distributional shift
options.text: Distributional shift
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the five concrete safety problems.

forms.stemHtml: Which term names a system's tendency to accept correction and shutdown from the people responsible for it instead of resisting them?

options.html: Situational awareness
options.text: Situational awareness
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on alignment and control.

options.html: Specification gaming
options.text: Specification gaming
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on alignment and control.

options.html: Corrigibility
options.text: Corrigibility
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A corrigible system accepts correction and shutdown, which limits the damage if its goals turn out to be wrong.

options.html: Distributional shift
options.text: Distributional shift
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on alignment and control.

forms.stemHtml: A criminal uses an AI model, working as designed, to write malicious code for a cyberattack. In the three categories used by the International AI Safety Report, which kind of risk is it?

options.html: Misuse
options.text: Misuse
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Misuse is the deliberate use of AI systems to cause harm. The system didn't fail; a person pointed it at a harmful end.

options.html: Malfunction
options.text: Malfunction
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on misuse, malfunction, and systemic risk.

options.html: Systemic risk
options.text: Systemic risk
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on misuse, malfunction, and systemic risk.

options.html: Evaluation awareness
options.text: Evaluation awareness
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on misuse, malfunction, and systemic risk.

forms.stemHtml: The UK AI Security Institute reported that it had found jailbreaks for every system it tested, and that breaking one newer model took far more expert effort than breaking an older one. What do these two findings show together?

options.html: Safeguards on newer models can no longer be broken at all
options.text: Safeguards on newer models can no longer be broken at all
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on safety evaluations.

options.html: Safeguards have made no measurable progress across models
options.text: Safeguards have made no measurable progress across models
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on safety evaluations.

options.html: Safeguards matter less now that models can recognize tests
options.text: Safeguards matter less now that models can recognize tests
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on safety evaluations.

options.html: Safeguards can improve and still be breakable by experts
options.text: Safeguards can improve and still be breakable by experts
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Every system's safeguards were broken, and the effort required rose sharply between two models. Both facts hold at once.

forms.stemHtml: In the 2025 blackmail scenario study, models wrote messages threatening to expose an executive's affair. Which statements about the study are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The models had many acceptable alternatives to choose from
options.text: The models had many acceptable alternatives to choose from
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on laboratory findings of deceptive behavior.

options.html: The company and the executive were fictional
options.text: The company and the executive were fictional
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The researchers invented the company, the emails, and the people in them.

options.html: Sixteen models from several developers were tested
options.text: Sixteen models from several developers were tested
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The models came from several companies, and models from all of them showed the behavior at some rate.

options.html: The authors said they had not seen such behavior in real deployments
options.text: The authors said they had not seen such behavior in real deployments
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! They state this directly, along with the fact that the scenario limited the models' options.

forms.stemHtml: Researchers who ran scheming studies and researchers who criticized them disagree about what the results mean. What do both sides accept?

options.html: The behaviors occur in the tests
options.text: The behaviors occur in the tests
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Both sides accept that models produced the reported outputs in the test scenarios. They dispute what this indicates about real use and future systems.

options.html: The behaviors occur often in ordinary use
options.text: The behaviors occur often in ordinary use
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the critique of scheming research.

options.html: The behaviors prove that models have intentions
options.text: The behaviors prove that models have intentions
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the critique of scheming research.

options.html: The behaviors show that the tests are worthless
options.text: The behaviors show that the tests are worthless
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the critique of scheming research.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these have interpretability researchers reported finding? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Internal patterns that match recognizable concepts
options.text: Internal patterns that match recognizable concepts
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Researchers call these features.

options.html: A case where a model's account of its reasoning differed from its internal process
options.text: A case where a model's account of its reasoning differed from its internal process
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A model described the school method for addition while its internal activity showed a different process.

options.html: Intermediate steps traced inside a model on selected prompts
options.text: Intermediate steps traced inside a model on selected prompts
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! One example is a model representing a state as a step toward naming its capital.

options.html: A complete map of everything a model does
options.text: A complete map of everything a model does
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on interpretability as safety evidence.

forms.stemHtml: Which position holds that a sufficiently capable system with the wrong goals might not be correctable, so that a mistake could be irreversible?

options.html: Normal technology
options.text: Normal technology
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the catastrophic-risk position.

options.html: Catastrophic risk
options.text: Catastrophic risk
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Advocates argue that unlike most technologies, this one might not allow repair after a mistake, up to the extinction of humanity.

options.html: Abundance
options.text: Abundance
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the catastrophic-risk position.

options.html: Intelligence explosion
options.text: Intelligence explosion
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the catastrophic-risk position.

forms.stemHtml: Which statements about the disputes that separate forecasts of AI's future are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The authors of a prominent short-timeline scenario later revised their forecasts in both directions
options.text: The authors of a prominent short-timeline scenario later revised their forecasts in both directions
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! They moved their estimates later and then earlier within about a year.

options.html: Whether automating AI research would produce runaway progress is disputed
options.text: Whether automating AI research would produce runaway progress is disputed
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! One side finds a self-reinforcing loop plausible, and another says the data are too thin to tell.

options.html: Computing power may limit how much additional researchers can speed progress
options.text: Computing power may limit how much additional researchers can speed progress
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! If ideas must be tested in large experiments, computing power is a bottleneck.

options.html: Expert surveys have settled how likely human extinction is
options.text: Expert surveys have settled how likely human extinction is
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on where the forecasts diverge.

title: Safety and Alignment
